This is essentially how we approached it last year, except they’re separating Origination and Trading this time. Regarding Assistants—we need to set the bonus targets rather than let OOC decide unilaterally. For non-commercial roles, we must provide clear targets as well, per our discussion earlier this week.

The biggest challenge remains integrating GCS and eliminating the manual Excel-GCS-Excel loop we struggled with last year. We’re collaborating with Hannah Ferguson and the GCS team to streamline this.

VPs will still go through the final firm-wide [LOC_1] review, adding an extra step. The [UNIT_1] meeting outcomes must align with the firm’s overall rating distribution (e.g., 10/80/10, 1-100 scale).

Jennifer

Here is our plan on West Region staffing.

Assistants:

Ranked 1,2,3 by supervisors - pay determined by Me and Brandy. No meetings.

Non Commercial but in North Division:

Traditional ranking with the correct people attending the meetings. Pay grid determined by OOC.

Analysts and Associates

Ranked as per Cameron Lemmons %'s and then pay grid determined by OOC  
I would like to see 25% - 65% - 10%. Cameron disagrees. This would provide for a quick meeting rather than trying to split them into 4 groups with the top one excluding some awesome people.

Managers/Directors

Ranked from 1 to 100 in as many clusters as the groups see fit. We are going to combine managers and directors into one table. The ranking is based on this years performance is directly related to pay. We will have two meetingss - one for traders and one for other commercial staff (orig/finance/etc). We will not have a pay prc but will take the results of the rankings and work with individual leaders after the meetings to ensure the appropriate compensation.

We will also determine promotions during this meeting using different criteria.

VP's

We will rank all our VP's from 1 to 100 with a group of selected people - some VP's and some MD's.  
This too will be directly related to pay.

Cheers as you Brits say
